articles.title: Modi Becomes the First Indian PM to Visit Slovakia. The People Who Waited Up for Him Were the Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: On a historic first visit since Slovakia's 1993 independence, India and Slovakia upgraded ties to a Comprehensive Partnership and signed defence and trade deals — but it was the airport crowd of Indian workers that captured the moment.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico at Bratislava Castle.
articles.nri_angle: The first-ever visit by an Indian PM to Slovakia signals that Central Europe is becoming a real destination for Indian skilled workers, and that India's consular and trade support is beginning to follow the diaspora to smaller, non-traditional countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Calls Anti-India Racism the Work of 'Stupid People.' For the Diaspora, the Visa Answer Mattered More.
articles.excerpt: At a New Delhi presser with Jaishankar, the US Secretary of State downplayed hate aimed at Indian-Americans while admitting the visa overhaul will create 'friction points' for the students and H-1B workers who form the diaspora's backbone.
articles.image_caption: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar.
articles.nri_angle: Rubio's 'stupid people' remark on anti-India racism went viral, but his admission that the J-1, F-1 and H-1B overhaul will create 'friction points' is what directly affects Indian students and tech workers in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Just Doubled Dollar Deposit Rates for NRIs to 7%. The RBI Is Footing the Risk.
articles.excerpt: To defend a sliding rupee, the Reserve Bank is absorbing the hedging cost on three-to-five-year FCNR deposits — letting banks pay NRIs 6 to 7.1 percent on dollars, more than double the old rate. The catch: the window closes September 30.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai, which is subsidising hedging costs to draw NRI dollar deposits.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn 6-7.1% on dollar-denominated FCNR deposits in Indian banks — more than double the old rate, with the currency risk underwritten by the RBI and the interest tax-free in India — but only on US-dollar deposits booked before September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Dismantled Birth Tourism Networks. The Real Worry for Indian Families Is What Comes Next.
articles.excerpt: Washington revoked hundreds of visas tied to overseas birth tourism rings. But the rhetoric driving the crackdown is the same one aimed at narrowing birthright citizenship for the children of H-1B holders — and the Supreme Court rules within weeks.
articles.image_caption: The Harry S. Truman Building, headquarters of the US State Department in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: The same campaign powering the birth tourism crackdown is being used to argue that US-born children of H-1B and student-visa holders — overwhelmingly Indian — should not be automatic citizens, with a Supreme Court ruling due within weeks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Trump Meet Wednesday for the First Time in 16 Months. H-1B Visas Are on the Table.
articles.excerpt: The two leaders hold their first face-to-face bilateral since February 2025 on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian. Trade and energy lead the agenda — but for the diaspora, the visa conversation is the one that counts.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at an earlier bilateral meeting
articles.nri_angle: Modi is expected to raise H-1B visas directly with Trump — the status that anchors the careers, mortgages and futures of millions of Indian professionals in the US, and which has lurched with every recent court ruling and policy pilot.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Struck Down Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Indian Tech Workers Are the Biggest Winners.
articles.excerpt: U.S. District Judge Leo Sorokin ruled the charge an unauthorised tax that only Congress could impose — lifting, for now, the steepest barrier ever placed in front of the visa that carries 70 percent of its approvals to Indian nationals.
articles.image_caption: The John Joseph Moakley federal courthouse in Boston, where Judge Leo Sorokin struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee
articles.nri_angle: Indians receive more than 70 percent of approved H-1B petitions each year, so a court striking down the $100,000 fee directly reopens the lower-cost path that built the Indian-American tech community — but with a PROTECT Act bill, a conflicting ruling, and appeals looming, the relief is provisional and every prospective applicant must weigh that the barrier could return.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Are Days From a Trade Deal. Their Top Negotiator Lands in Delhi on June 23.
articles.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer will visit New Delhi to finalise the first tranche of a bilateral pact that aims to double trade to $500 billion — even as May exports jumped 18 percent and Washington floats fresh tariffs on Indian textiles and steel.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who travels to New Delhi on June 23 to finalize the interim India-US trade pact (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A US-India trade pact shapes the rupee-dollar rate that determines the real value of every remittance and NRE deposit, lifts the Indian exporters and small businesses whose fortunes ripple back through diaspora family and investment networks, and signals a warming bilateral climate that historically eases the visa and mobility rules governing how NRIs move between the two countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: No More Flying Home to Renew a Visa: The US Will Pilot Domestic H-1B Renewals in December, Mostly for Indians
articles.excerpt: The State Department will issue 20,000 visas over three months to holders already in the country, ending the dreaded renewal trip for thousands — and officials say the vast majority of the first group will be Indian nationals.
articles.image_caption: The U.S. State Department headquarters in Washington; a December pilot will let many H-1B holders renew visas domestically (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the largest group of skilled workers in the US and have borne the worst of consular backlogs, so a domestic H-1B renewal pilot — 20,000 slots from December, mostly for Indian nationals — ends the forced, months-long renewal trip home that has separated diaspora families from their jobs, and frees India's missions to clear the queues facing first-time student and worker applicants.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Are Now the Most Deported Nationality From Canada. The Numbers Are Not Close.
articles.excerpt: CBSA data shows 1,712 Indian citizens removed in the first quarter of 2026 — nearly one in three of all deportations — with another 6,980 cases pending, the largest single-country backlog on record.
articles.image_caption: Interior of Toronto Pearson International Airport; Indians are now the most-deported nationality from Canada (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indians are Canada's largest international student and temporary-worker population, so a removals surge that has pushed them to the top of the CBSA's deportation list — 1,712 in Q1 2026, with 6,980 cases pending — lands directly on the same study-to-PR pipeline that drew them, a warning that the margin for any lapse in status has collapsed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three Indian-Americans Has Thought About Leaving the US. The Arrow Is Now Pointing Both Ways.
articles.excerpt: A Carnegie Endowment survey finds the community that defined the American success story is quietly weighing the exits — driven by political alienation, cost of living, and an endless wait for green cards — just as a more confident India draws its talent home.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons (CC)
articles.nri_angle: When the United States' most successful immigrant community — 5.2 million strong, Silicon Valley's backbone — starts treating migration as a global optimization problem rather than a one-way move, it reshapes the calculus for every NRI weighing whether to stay, leave, or return, and signals that belonging built on economic usefulness has limits even at the very top.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Ready to Break Its Own Budget Promise. The Reason Is Sitting in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi will let its fiscal deficit widen to as much as 4.8 percent of GDP — above February's 4.3 percent target — as the Gulf war drives up energy and fertiliser subsidy costs, even as a fragile peace deal offers the first hint of relief.
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, who warned of uncertainty over forex, oil and fertiliser prices and a rain shortfall
articles.nri_angle: A wider Indian deficit and an uncertain rupee directly shape what NRIs earn on NRE/NRO deposits, property, and bonds back home — and the RBI's push to plug the gap by courting overseas money, including new hedging benefits on non-resident deposits, is aimed squarely at the diaspora's savings, making the value of every remittance and investment hinge on whether this fiscal bet holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Opendoor Just Closed Its Entire India Operation. The Reason Wasn't Cost — It Was AI.
articles.excerpt: The US real-estate firm laid off 250 employees in Chennai and Bengaluru, saying AI-native US teams can now absorb the work. Analysts warn it's a preview of what's coming for India's back-office economy.
articles.image_caption: A technology company's headquarters in Bengaluru, India's GCC capital
articles.nri_angle: India's $100 billion Global Capability Center economy gave millions their first job; when US firms cite AI rather than cost to pull work back onshore, the entry-level roles that anchor diaspora families and feed the H-1B pipeline are the first to vanish.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Renamed the One Tax Form Every Salaried Person Knows. Form 16 Is Now Form 130.
articles.excerpt: The decades-old salary TDS certificate gets a three-part redesign and a new statutory basis under the Income-tax Act, 2025 — and for NRIs filing from abroad, every familiar form they rely on has quietly been relabelled.
articles.image_caption: India's Income Tax Department has renamed the salaried taxpayer's return form (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs with salary, rent, or financial ties in India rely on forms like Form 16, Form 16A and Form 26AS to file from abroad without an accountant — and the Income-tax Act, 2025 has renamed all of them at once (to Form 130, 131 and 168), making the 2026-27 tax year a minefield of paperwork confusion even though the underlying liability is unchanged.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: British Commandos Seized a Russian Shadow-Fleet Tanker. The Captain They Charged Is Indian.
articles.excerpt: Ajay Pant, 38, faces up to ten years in a UK prison for breaching sanctions — a case that exposes how India's vast merchant-seafarer workforce is being drawn, often unknowingly, into the most legally dangerous corner of global shipping.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea, the kind of vessel that crews Russia's sanctioned shadow fleet (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indians are one of the largest national groups among the world's merchant seafarers, and the charging of Captain Ajay Pant shows how that workforce — long celebrated by India for its remittances but rarely protected — is being pulled into the Russian shadow fleet, where the Indian officer on the bridge, not the hidden beneficial owner, is the one who ends up in handcuffs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Are Now Australia's Largest Migrant Group. That Is Exactly Why They Are Under Attack.
articles.excerpt: A milestone of belonging has collided with a wave of anti-immigration protests — and researchers warn that the 'model minority' label Indian-Australians wear with pride offers no protection when politics turns against them.
articles.image_caption: Sydney, Australia, where Indians have become the largest overseas-born community for the first time
articles.nri_angle: Indians becoming Australia's largest overseas-born community is a milestone of belonging that also makes them the most visible target of rising anti-immigration sentiment — and the lesson, that acceptance built on economic usefulness is fragile and conditional, applies to the entire 35-million-strong global diaspora from Britain to Canada to the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The War That Choked India's Oil Lifeline May Be Ending. New Delhi Welcomes the US-Iran Gulf Deal.
articles.excerpt: A framework agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz sent crude tumbling 5 percent and lifted the rupee — a rare piece of good macro news for the world's third-largest oil importer and the nine million Indians in the Gulf.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons (CC)
articles.nri_angle: The Gulf hosts roughly nine million Indians — the world's largest diaspora concentration — and India is the third-largest oil importer, so a ceasefire that reopens the Strait of Hormuz directly affects remittance values, NRI deposit returns, Indian markets, and the daily lives of millions of Indian workers who endured months of evacuations and closed airspaces.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 9.27 Lakh Indians Brought Home From a War Zone. Inside India's Largest Peacetime Evacuation.
articles.excerpt: Special flights, reopened airspaces and overland convoys through Armenia and Azerbaijan have carried nearly a million Indians out of West Asia — a real-time test of the promise the Indian state makes to its citizens abroad.
articles.image_caption: North and South Block in New Delhi, where India's Ministry of External Affairs coordinates the West Asia repatriation effort
articles.nri_angle: The Gulf hosts roughly nine million Indians — mostly workers whose remittances sustain families back home — and the MEA's evacuation of 9.27 lakh people via flights and overland routes through the Caucasus is a direct test of India's duty to protect its diaspora when war closes the skies, shaping how secure the next generation of migrants feels about working abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Markets Just Got the One Thing Money Can't Buy: an End to War. The Diaspora Is Being Asked to Help.
articles.excerpt: The Sensex and Nifty rallied nearly 3 percent in two sessions as the Gulf peace deal sank oil — even as the RBI and banks hike NRI deposit rates to 7 percent to pull dollars back after a record $30 billion foreign exodus.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, where the Sensex rallied on news of the Gulf peace deal
articles.nri_angle: The RBI and banks have hiked NRI and FCNR deposit rates to 6-7.1 percent — beating most Western savings products — while absorbing currency-hedging risk, so for the diaspora this is a rare moment when patriotism and self-interest align: India is explicitly asking overseas Indians to anchor its finances after a record $30 billion foreign exodus, and the cheap rupee and post-war market rebound make it a compelling entry point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Bet $150 Million on India Building Its Own AI. Sarvam Is Now Worth $1.5 Billion.
articles.excerpt: The IT giant's 10.5 percent stake in the three-year-old startup is a wager that India's 'sovereign AI' future will be built in Bengaluru, not rented from Silicon Valley.
articles.image_caption: Servers powering artificial intelligence systems as India backs homegrown AI
articles.nri_angle: A huge share of the world's AI talent is of Indian origin and many NRIs are angel investors and LPs in the very funds backing Sarvam — so a credible, well-capitalised Indian AI champion creates a real reverse-migration and investment pull for the diaspora to build in and invest in India rather than only abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Just Put 120 Indian Startups in Front of the World's Investors. The Pitch: Innovate With India.
articles.excerpt: Bharat Innovates 2026 opened in Nice with a deliberate message — India wants to be seen as a creator of technology, not a consumer of it, and the diaspora is its target audience.
articles.image_caption: PM Narendra Modi, who co-launched Bharat Innovates 2026 with France's Emmanuel Macron in Nice
articles.nri_angle: Many overseas Indians are now venture investors, corporate leaders and researchers — precisely the audience Bharat Innovates was built to court; the event is in effect an invitation to the diaspora to back the next generation of Indian deep-tech companies at the earliest stage and to be partners in India's rise rather than spectators.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Supreme Court Just Seized Control of the Fight Over Who Can Define a Person's Gender
articles.excerpt: The court stayed every High Court challenge to the Transgender Amendment Act 2026 and signalled it may decide itself whether the State can override the right to self-identify that it enshrined in 2014.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India, which stayed all High Court challenges to the Transgender Amendment Act 2026
articles.nri_angle: India's NALSA judgment is cited worldwide as a landmark in transgender rights, and transgender OCI/PIO holders who travel to or settle in India would face the new law's medical-certification regime — so for the diaspora, and especially its LGBTQ+ members, the case is a barometer of whether the homeland's constitutional rights gains are durable or reversible.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Pulled a Record ₹2.87 Lakh Crore From Indian Stocks. Wall Street Is Quietly Betting They Will Come Back.
articles.excerpt: FPIs yanked ₹62,853 crore from equities in just 15 days of June — but Morgan Stanley, Goldman and others argue India's absence from the AI frenzy has left it oversold and primed for a rebound.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where foreign investors have pulled out a record sum in 2026
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs hold Indian equities and mutual funds, and the RBI's new deposit and bond incentives target diaspora dollars directly — so the record FPI exodus versus Wall Street's contrarian rebound thesis frames a real decision for diaspora investors: treat the outflows as a warning, or as a capitulation bottom.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Money Is Now Tracked Monthly. The First Snapshot Shows Diaspora Remittances Surging as Foreign Investors Flee.
articles.excerpt: The RBI's new monthly balance of payments data revealed an April deficit driven by capital outflows — even as remittances from overseas Indians jumped to $16 billion, up from $9.4 billion a year ago.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India in Mumbai, which began publishing monthly balance of payments data
articles.nri_angle: The April data makes the diaspora's collective financial weight visible: as foreign portfolio investors pulled out $11.3 billion, remittances from overseas Indians surged to $16 billion — a counter-cyclical, rupee-stabilising flow that is increasingly the ballast holding up India's external accounts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dubai and Singapore Have Long Held NRI Money. GIFT City Is Now Making a Serious Bid to Bring It Home.
articles.excerpt: With the first Foreign Family Investment Fund approved and Singaporean capital flowing in, India's IFSC at GIFT City is positioning itself as a tax-efficient, India-linked base for diaspora wealth.
articles.image_caption: GIFT City near Gandhinagar, India's first International Financial Services Centre
articles.nri_angle: GIFT City offers NRIs a tax-efficient, India-linked base for family offices, offshore funds and succession planning — letting the diaspora invest in India's growth without the friction of onshore structures or the geopolitical concentration risk of a single foreign hub.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Britain Is Rewriting Its Immigration Rulebook. For Indians — Its Biggest Migrant Group — One Door Opens as Several Narrow.
articles.excerpt: A CETA trade-deal route could let Indian professionals work in the UK for up to a year, even as tougher English tests, a shorter graduate visa and a new student levy raise the cost of British migration.
articles.image_caption: Westminster, London; the UK is reshaping visa and settlement rules that affect Indian migrants
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the UK's largest migrant group — the biggest source of work visas and among the largest of students — so every shift in British visa, settlement and trade-deal mobility rules directly reshapes the plans of diaspora families studying, working or settling in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Gulf Crisis Just Reached India's Fields. Sixteen Fertiliser Ships Are Stranded in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.excerpt: With 330,000 tons of urea and 257,000 tons of DAP stuck in contested waters, New Delhi insists the summer sowing season is safe — even as it floats fresh import tenders to plug the gap.
articles.image_caption: The bulk carrier Darya Ganga; 16 India-bound ships carrying fertiliser are stranded in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.nri_angle: Many NRIs remit money to farming families, own agricultural land, or track India's rural economy — and a fertiliser shortfall at sowing time means higher food inflation, squeezed rural incomes and added pressure on the remittances that cushion millions of households back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Its Sailors to Stop Going Into the Gulf. Three Were Just Killed There.
articles.excerpt: After the MT Settebello strike off Oman, the Directorate General of Shipping has restricted Indian seafarer deployment to conflict zones — a rare operational step as families demand more than protests.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, where Indian-crewed vessels have come under attack

sources.label: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers make up ~12% of the global maritime workforce; their remittances sustain coastal and northern Indian households, and the Gulf is their most-trafficked and now most-dangerous corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The World's Tech Giants Are Building in Bengaluru, Not Hiring in California. India's GCC Workforce Is Headed for 2.36 Million.
articles.excerpt: As US visa policy tightens, multinationals are pouring high-end AI and cybersecurity work into India-based capability centres. N-able's new Bengaluru hub is the latest sign of where global tech is moving.
articles.image_caption: The Bengaluru skyline, India's premier technology hub and centre of its GCC boom
articles.nri_angle: As H-1B fees rise and green-card backlogs stretch decades, GCCs let Indian engineers build global careers without emigrating — reshaping the calculus NRIs and their families make about returning home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Students Crashed the US Visa Portal on Day One. The Embassy Says Thousands More Slots Are Coming.
articles.excerpt: After the June 14 reopening triggered a frantic rush and technical glitches, the US Embassy in India assured applicants that more appointments for July and August will open in the coming weeks.
articles.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi, which reopened student visa appointment scheduling this week
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are the largest group of international students in the US and the front of the diaspora pipeline — today's F-1 applicants become tomorrow's H-1B workers, green-card holders and citizens.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Germany Just Scrapped the Airport Transit Visa for Indians. Frankfurt and Munich Are Now Open Gateways.
articles.excerpt: From June 3, Indian passport holders can connect through German airports to non-Schengen destinations without a Type A transit visa. The fine print still matters.
articles.image_caption: Jorbasa via flickr (BY-ND)
articles.nri_angle: Frankfurt and Munich are among the busiest connecting hubs for Indians flying to North America, so scrapping the transit visa directly eases travel for NRIs, students and visiting families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 23 Died in a Delhi B&B That Should Never Have Been Open. The Inspector Who Cleared It Has Been Sacked.
articles.excerpt: A six-room licence, 25 rooms in reality, sealed windows and no fire NOC. As Delhi promises a citywide crackdown, critics ask why a cook was arrested before the owners and officials.
articles.image_caption: A Delhi Fire Service engine responds to an emergency (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI families visiting India for medical care, weddings and pilgrimages routinely stay in exactly the kind of budget, informally regulated lodgings that turned deadly in Malviya Nagar.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Mother Can Now Get Her Child an Indian Passport Without the Father's Signature. The Andhra Court Just Said So.
articles.excerpt: Justice Battu Devanand ruled that the prescribed declarations are enough — no paternal consent required. It joins a growing line of high court judgments protecting single parents.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport; courts have repeatedly affirmed a single parent's right to obtain one for a minor

sources.label: Andhra Pradesh High Court (Shaik Shabana v. Union of India)
Telangana High Court / Child Rights Clinic

articles.nri_angle: Cross-border custody and long-distance separations are common in NRI families; the ruling gives single parents abroad a clear path to obtain a child's passport without an uncooperative ex's signature.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Has Rewritten Its Immigration Rulebook for 2026. Here Is What It Means for Indians.
articles.excerpt: Ottawa slashed generic temporary visas by 43 percent and made occupation-based draws the core of Express Entry. For Indian professionals, a high score is no longer enough — only a precise sector fit gets you in.
articles.image_caption: Parliament Hill in Ottawa, where Canada sets the immigration policy reshaping its Express Entry system for 2026
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the single largest source of Canadian Express Entry invitations, and the 2026 overhaul reshapes the most reliable migration route out of India away from the American green card backlog.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pay $750 and Skip the U.S. Visa Line. For Indian Families, the New Fee Cuts Both Ways.
articles.excerpt: From July 1, B-1/B-2 applicants can buy an interview within ten business days for $750 on top of the standard fee. It is relief for families facing year-long waits at Indian consulates — and a new equity problem.
articles.image_caption: U.S. visa processing now carries a new surcharge for visitors (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian consulates post some of the world's longest visitor-visa waits, so the expedite fee directly affects NRIs trying to bring parents and family to the US for births, weddings, and graduations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: El Nino Is Here. India's Monsoon Season Faces Its Biggest Threat in a Decade.
articles.excerpt: U.S. and Indian forecasters have confirmed El Nino conditions that could slash rainfall, shrink harvests, and push food prices higher as 200 million rain-fed farming households begin sowing.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: NRI families in agricultural states face higher food prices and increased remittance demand as a weak monsoon threatens rural incomes and consumption.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kevin Warsh Chairs His First Fed Meeting This Week. Here Is Why NRIs Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: The new Federal Reserve chairman presides over a pivotal policy decision on Wednesday as inflation climbs, rate hike odds rise, and every signal from Washington ripples through India's rupee, bond markets, and NRI investment portfolios.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers remarks at his swearing-in ceremony at the White House, May 22, 2026
articles.nri_angle: NRIs face direct consequences from the Fed's rate path — from U.S. mortgage rates and investment returns to rupee exchange rates and the attractiveness of India-bound deposit schemes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The G7 Has Opened in Evian. Iran, Trade, and India's Seat at the Table Are All in Play.
articles.excerpt: Modi arrives at the French lakeside summit with a dense agenda: the Iran peace deal, a Trump bilateral on Wednesday, and the visa question that won't go away.
articles.image_caption: World leaders at a G7 summit group photo
articles.nri_angle: The G7 agenda — Iran oil prices, US-India trade talks, and H-1B visa policy — directly shapes the economic and immigration landscape for millions of NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Markets Surge as Iran Peace Deal Sends Oil Below $84 and Revives Inflow Hopes.
articles.excerpt: Nifty jumps 1.5 per cent, rupee heads for 94.80, and BlackRock says India's $30 billion selloff was overdone. Here is what NRIs should know.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: RBI's new FCNR deposit window and a strengthening rupee make NRI remittances and property investments cheaper — if the oil price drop holds.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gujarat Has Launched Its Industrial Policy 2026. It Wants Semiconductor Factories, Ultra Mega Projects, and NRI Capital.
articles.excerpt: The state expands its priority sectors from nine to sixteen, creates a new category for ₹10,000 crore investments, and puts green manufacturing at the centre of its pitch.
articles.image_caption: Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel at an official event
articles.nri_angle: Gujarat's semiconductor push, green manufacturing incentives, and GIFT City expansion create new investment channels for the state's 10-million-strong global diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Deploy Air Force Planes to Guard Its Medical Exam. Here Is How the NEET Scandal Unravelled.
articles.excerpt: The CBI has arrested 13 people, a headmistress confessed to leaking the physics paper, and 22 lakh students must now retake the test under military-grade security on June 21.
articles.image_caption: An Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft — the IAF is being tasked with ferrying NEET exam papers to prevent leaks (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI families with children or relatives preparing for medical entrance exams face uncertainty about the integrity of India's examination system.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Factories Are Losing 40 Per Cent of Their Output to Heat. The Economic Cost Could Hit 4.5 Per Cent of GDP.
articles.excerpt: In Kanpur, workers are collapsing or returning to their villages. New research shows the growth hit from rising temperatures is nearly double what economists previously believed.
articles.image_caption: Workers in an Indian factory — extreme heat is cutting factory output by up to 40 per cent across the country (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with investments in Indian manufacturing and families back home face growing risks from a heat crisis that is cutting factory output and threatening the health of vulnerable relatives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Has Cut Off India From Anthropic's Best AI. Bengaluru Is Building Its Own.
articles.excerpt: The US blocked Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals. India's Sarvam AI has raised $300 million and trained a 105-billion-parameter model for Indian languages. The sovereign AI race is on.
articles.image_caption: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, whose most advanced AI models are now restricted from export to India (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian technologists in the US face export controls based on nationality, while NRI investors see a new asset class emerging in India's sovereign AI ecosystem.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi Is Taking the Exam Scandal Fight to Kota. Here Is What Congress Is Demanding.
articles.excerpt: A nationwide campaign against paper leaks and CBSE failures starts on June 17, with student conventions planned across four cities. The party wants NEET decentralised and the education minister gone.
articles.image_caption: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, who will lead student conventions starting June 17 in Kota
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of NRI and OCI students sit for CBSE board exams and NEET every year — a compromised examination system directly threatens the merit-based pathway that diaspora families count on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US-Iran Deal Is Done. Oil Has Dropped 4 Per Cent. Here Is What It Means for India.
articles.excerpt: The Strait of Hormuz will reopen immediately. The naval blockade is over. A signing ceremony is set for Friday in Switzerland. And India's oil import bill just got significantly lighter.
articles.image_caption: Map of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman that carries a fifth of the world's oil
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper crude oil means a stronger rupee, lower petrol prices in India, and relief for NRIs watching the currency slide all year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Will Build a 168-Megawatt AI Data Centre Inside Ambani's Jamnagar Complex. Here Is Why It Matters.
articles.excerpt: The deal deepens Meta's partnership with Reliance, positions India as an AI infrastructure hub, and arrives just as Anthropic's access restrictions have reignited the sovereign AI debate.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, whose Jamnagar complex will host Meta's new AI data centre
articles.nri_angle: India's AI infrastructure is moving from government promises to concrete projects — creating high-skilled jobs, boosting Jio Platforms' IPO profile, and potentially reducing dependence on foreign AI providers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Have Drawn Up a Five-Year Plan to Double Trade. Here Is Everything They Agreed at Villa Kerylos.
articles.excerpt: An Innovation Roadmap 2030, a joint AI working group, a new dialogue on critical minerals, and 19 signed agreements — the Nice summit delivered substance, not just ceremony.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron during a bilateral meeting
articles.nri_angle: The bilateral outcomes directly affect NRIs through visa-free French airport transit, expanded education pathways, and a trade mechanism that could reshape India's commercial access to all 27 EU member states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Tech Leaders Are Demanding a $6 Billion AI Fund. The Anthropic Shutdown Made It Personal.
articles.excerpt: Mohandas Pai wants ₹50,000 crore a year for sovereign AI. Sridhar Vembu says go open-source. Both agree on one thing: India cannot build its future on infrastructure it does not control.
articles.image_caption: India's top tech leaders are demanding a sovereign AI fund after Anthropic's service restrictions in India exposed the country's dependence on foreign AI providers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers on H-1B visas at U.S. AI companies are now classified alongside all foreign nationals under the new export controls — making this both a policy story and a personal one for the diaspora workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Now Under Fire From Both Sides in the Gulf. The U.S. Struck Its Sailors. Trump Says Iran Attacked Its Ships Too.
articles.excerpt: Three Indian seafarers are dead from a U.S. Navy strike. Hours later, Trump accused Iran of launching drones at Indian vessels. Jaishankar called Rubio to protest. India's 300,000 merchant sailors are caught in the middle of a war they played no part in starting.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who called U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to lodge a strong protest over the killing of Indian sailors
articles.nri_angle: India is the world's second-largest supplier of merchant seafarers — over 300,000 globally. Many NRI families in coastal states have relatives working on vessels in the Gulf, and the escalating attacks have triggered panic across the maritime community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Judge Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. Four Days Later, He Froze His Own Ruling.
articles.excerpt: The legal seesaw has left Indian tech workers in limbo as Trump appeals and Congress moves to codify the fee permanently.
articles.image_caption: Judge Leo Sorokin, who ruled the $100,000 H-1B fee unconstitutional
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for over 70% of all H-1B petitions — the fee's fate directly determines whether hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals can afford to work in the United States.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Waived Customs Duty on Nuclear Equipment Going Back Seven Years. The Market Noticed.
articles.excerpt: The retrospective exemption formalises an unwritten practice, cuts project costs, and sends nuclear stocks surging as India chases 100 GW by 2047.
articles.image_caption: A nuclear power plant in India — the government has waived customs duty on equipment imports going back seven years
articles.nri_angle: The nuclear duty waiver and 100 GW target create a multi-decade infrastructure investment opportunity for NRIs tracking India's energy transition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
